_comment_1: Acceptance policy for the signoff STA gate. There are TWO kinds of value in here and they must not be confused.
_comment_2: REQUIREMENTS. What a signed-off chip must satisfy. These are NOT observations and must never be relaxed to match a run. The design currently FAILS these, which is correct: it does not close timing.
_comment_3: TRIPWIRES. These ARE pinned to a measured baseline, deliberately. Their job is change detection - to notice a clock or a view disappearing between P&R and STA - not to assert that the baseline is right. Pinning a requirement to today's number would be back-fitting; pinning a structural tripwire is the only way it can work.
_comment_4: clock count: the SDC defines 33 clocks (4 create_clock + 29 create_generated_clock) but the loaded database reports 66. That discrepancy is UNEXPLAINED as of 2026-08-18 and is an open question, not a settled fact. The tripwire is set to the database number because that is what STA actually analyses. If you resolve the 33-vs-66 question, update this AND the note in docs/tapeout/40-signoff-sta-plan.md.
_comment_5: Signing off on exactly one setup corner and one hold corner is a DECISION (D3 in the plan doc), not a default. Listed here so that a view silently vanishing is caught. Adding corners can only find more violations.
_comment_6: Extraction quality. require_qrc_all_rc_corners fails the gate if any RC corner falls back to cap-table-only extraction, which is how a 65nm design silently gets effort-level 'low' parasitics (IMPEXT-3518).
_comment_7: Analysis mode. Both of these are re-issued by run_signoff_sta.tcl rather than inherited, because the routed DB persists derate for typical_delay_corner ONLY - neither signoff corner. A run that inherits reports better timing than the flow did.
